context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task. Deep creative work may need longer uninterrupted periods, so some people adjust the length to 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute break. The technique also encourages tracking. At the end of each day the learner counts how many pomodoros were completed, which gives a simple measure of effort.

This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins. If a distraction appears during a pomodoro, the worker writes it down on a separate list and returns to the task at once. A pomodoro that is interrupted cannot be counted, and it must be restarted from the beginning. Language learners use the method to study vocabulary, grammar or listening in short focused blocks. Many find that the fixed limit makes it easier to start, because the task feels smaller than a whole evening of study. Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task.
answer: The Pomodoro Technique was developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s.

context: Word Families and Affixes A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. Learning a whole family at once is more efficient than learning each word separately. Most word families are built from a base word plus affixes. There are two kinds of affixes: prefixes, which come before the base, and suffixes, which come after it. For example, in the word unhappiness, un- is a prefix and -ness is a suffix. Prefixes usually change the meaning but not the part of speech. The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite.

Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text. Reaching 98 percent, which is considered comfortable for reading without a dictionary, requires about 8,000 to 9,000 word families. A common mistake is to assume that every affix works with every base. The word informal takes the prefix in-, but the correct opposites of possible and legal are impossible and illegal, because the prefix changes its spelling before the letters p and l. To practise, learners can choose a base word each day and write down as many family members as they can before checking a dictionary.

The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite. The prefix pre- means before, as in preview, and mis- means wrongly, as in misunderstand. Suffixes usually change the part of speech. The suffix -tion turns a verb into a noun, as in educate and education. The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb, as in quick and quickly, and -able makes an adjective from a verb, as in comfortable or readable. Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text.

context: The Shadowing Technique Shadowing is a language learning method in which the learner listens to a recording and repeats it aloud almost at the same time, staying only about one second behind the speaker. The method was popularised by the interpreter and professor Alexander Arguelles. The technique trains pronunciation, rhythm and intonation rather than vocabulary. Because the learner must copy the speaker's stress and pauses, the mouth muscles become used to the sounds of the language. There are two main forms. In no-text shadowing, the learner listens and repeats without reading anything. In text shadowing, the learner follows a transcript while speaking, which is easier and is recommended for beginners. A typical session has four steps.

Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly. Shadowing does not replace conversation. It improves accuracy of sound, but the learner still needs to speak with real people to practise choosing words quickly.

A typical session has four steps. First, listen to the audio once to understand the general meaning. Second, read the transcript and look up unknown words. Third, shadow the audio while reading the text. Fourth, shadow again without the text and record your own voice to compare it with the original. Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Clips of one to two minutes are long enough to be useful and short enough to repeat many times. Ten to fifteen minutes of daily practice is enough. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.
answer: The learner stays only about one second behind the speaker when shadowing.

Hai mệnh đề có thể đổi chỗ cho nhau; khi mệnh đề if đứng đầu câu thì ta đặt dấu phẩy sau nó. Câu điều kiện loại 1 diễn tả điều kiện có thể xảy ra ở hiện tại hoặc tương lai. Cấu trúc là If + thì hiện tại đơn, S + will + động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home. Câu điều kiện loại 2 diễn tả điều kiện không có thật ở hiện tại hoặc rất khó xảy ra.

Câu điều kiện loại 2 diễn tả điều kiện không có thật ở hiện tại hoặc rất khó xảy ra. Cấu trúc là If + thì quá khứ đơn, S + would + động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ: If I had a million dollars, I would travel around the world. Trong câu điều kiện loại 2, động từ to be ở mệnh đề if thường dùng dạng were cho mọi chủ ngữ, kể cả I, he và she. Vì vậy ta nói If I were you, I would apologise, chứ không nói If I was you trong văn phong trang trọng. Không dùng will hoặc would trong mệnh đề if.

Không dùng will hoặc would trong mệnh đề if. Câu If you will study hard, you pass là sai; câu đúng là If you study hard, you will pass. Ở mệnh đề chính, ngoài will và would ta có thể dùng các động từ khuyết thiếu khác như can, could, may hoặc might để diễn tả khả năng thấp hơn, ví dụ: If you practise every day, you might improve quickly. Từ unless có nghĩa là if not. Câu Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus có nghĩa giống như If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.

context: Từ dễ nhầm lẫn — Confusing words Nhiều người học nhầm lẫn các cặp từ có cách viết hoặc âm đọc gần giống nhau. Many learners confuse pairs of words that look or sound similar. affect và effect — Affect thường là động từ nghĩa là ảnh hưởng đến: The weather affects my mood. Effect thường là danh từ nghĩa là tác động: The medicine had a good effect. its và it's — Its là tính từ sở hữu: The cat licked its paw. It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining.

advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/. Advise là động từ, đọc là /ədˈvaɪz/. Ta nói give some advice, không nói give an advice. Cách học: hãy viết một câu ví dụ riêng cho mỗi từ trong cặp và đọc to câu đó. Writing one example sentence for each word helps you remember the difference better than memorising a definition.

It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining. their, there và they're — Their chỉ sự sở hữu của họ, there chỉ nơi chốn, còn they're là viết tắt của they are. Example: They're putting their bags over there. then và than — Then chỉ thời gian hoặc thứ tự: First we ate, then we left. Than dùng để so sánh: She is taller than her brother. lose và loose — Lose /luːz/ là động từ, nghĩa là mất hoặc thua: Don't lose your keys. Loose /luːs/ là tính từ, nghĩa là lỏng: This shirt is too loose. advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/.

context: Business Email Phrases — Cụm từ trong email công việc A professional email usually has five parts: a subject line, a greeting, an opening sentence, the main message and a closing. Một email công việc thường có năm phần: tiêu đề, lời chào, câu mở đầu, nội dung chính và lời kết. Subject line — Keep it under eight words and make it specific, for example Meeting request: project update on Thursday. Tiêu đề rõ ràng giúp người nhận quyết định mở thư nhanh hơn. Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together.

Tránh nói I attach the file without mentioning what it is. Nhớ kiểm tra tệp đính kèm trước khi bấm gửi. Closing — Best regards is the most common closing and is safe in most situations. Yours faithfully is used with Dear Sir or Madam, and Yours sincerely is used with a person's name. Thân mật hơn thì có thể dùng Kind regards. Tone — Avoid slang, capital letters for whole sentences and too many exclamation marks. Viết ngắn gọn: mỗi đoạn tối đa ba đến bốn câu. Before sending, read the email aloud once to check the tone and correct spelling mistakes.

Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together. If you do not know the name, write Dear Sir or Madam, though many companies now prefer Dear Hiring Team. Opening — I am writing to inquire about... (tôi viết thư để hỏi về...), Thank you for your prompt reply (cảm ơn bạn đã phản hồi nhanh). Requests — Could you please send me the report by Friday? is polite. Từ please và could làm câu yêu cầu lịch sự hơn so với Send me the report. Attachments — Please find the attached file. Tránh nói I attach the file without mentioning what it is.
answer: A professional email usually has five parts.

context: The IELTS Speaking Test The IELTS Speaking test is a face-to-face interview with a certified examiner and lasts between 11 and 14 minutes. It is recorded so that the result can be checked later. The test has three parts. In Part 1, which lasts four to five minutes, the examiner asks general questions about familiar topics such as home, family, work and hobbies. In Part 2 the candidate receives a task card with a topic and has one minute to prepare notes. The candidate then speaks for one to two minutes without interruption. The examiner stops the candidate after two minutes. Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes.

It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example. If a candidate does not understand a question, they may ask the examiner to repeat it, and this does not reduce the score. The speaking test can take place on the same day as the other sections or up to seven days before or after them.

Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes. The questions are more abstract and are connected to the topic in Part 2, for example asking the candidate to compare past and present or to predict the future. Four criteria are used for marking, and each is worth 25 percent of the score: fluency and coherence, lexical resource, grammatical range and accuracy, and pronunciation. Scores are given in bands from 0 to 9, and half bands such as 6.5 are allowed. Candidates are advised not to memorise answers, because examiners are trained to notice rehearsed language and it lowers the fluency score. It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example.

context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task. Deep creative work may need longer uninterrupted periods, so some people adjust the length to 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute break. The technique also encourages tracking. At the end of each day the learner counts how many pomodoros were completed, which gives a simple measure of effort.

This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins. If a distraction appears during a pomodoro, the worker writes it down on a separate list and returns to the task at once. A pomodoro that is interrupted cannot be counted, and it must be restarted from the beginning. Language learners use the method to study vocabulary, grammar or listening in short focused blocks. Many find that the fixed limit makes it easier to start, because the task feels smaller than a whole evening of study. Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task.

context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

context: Word Families and Affixes A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. Learning a whole family at once is more efficient than learning each word separately. Most word families are built from a base word plus affixes. There are two kinds of affixes: prefixes, which come before the base, and suffixes, which come after it. For example, in the word unhappiness, un- is a prefix and -ness is a suffix. Prefixes usually change the meaning but not the part of speech. The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite.

Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text. context: The Shadowing Technique Shadowing is a language learning method in which the learner listens to a recording and repeats it aloud almost at the same time, staying only about one second behind the speaker. The method was popularised by the interpreter and professor Alexander Arguelles. The technique trains pronunciation, rhythm and intonation rather than vocabulary. Because the learner must copy the speaker's stress and pauses, the mouth muscles become used to the sounds of the language. There are two main forms. In no-text shadowing, the learner listens and repeats without reading anything. In text shadowing, the learner follows a transcript while speaking, which is easier and is recommended for beginners. A typical session has four steps.

Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly. Shadowing does not replace conversation. It improves accuracy of sound, but the learner still needs to speak with real people to practise choosing words quickly.

A typical session has four steps. First, listen to the audio once to understand the general meaning. Second, read the transcript and look up unknown words. Third, shadow the audio while reading the text. Fourth, shadow again without the text and record your own voice to compare it with the original. Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Clips of one to two minutes are long enough to be useful and short enough to repeat many times. Ten to fifteen minutes of daily practice is enough. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.
answer: The learner stays only about one second behind the speaker [1].

context: Mạo từ a, an và the trong tiếng Anh Mạo từ là từ đứng trước danh từ để cho biết danh từ đó xác định hay không xác định. Tiếng Anh có hai loại mạo từ: mạo từ không xác định gồm a và an, và mạo từ xác định là the. Ta dùng a trước từ bắt đầu bằng phụ âm và an trước từ bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm. Điều quan trọng là âm đọc chứ không phải chữ cái viết: ta nói an hour vì chữ h không được đọc, và nói a university vì từ này bắt đầu bằng âm /j/.

Ví dụ: Water is essential for life và Dogs are loyal animals. Với tên các bữa ăn, môn thể thao và môn học ta thường bỏ mạo từ, như have breakfast, play football và study mathematics. context: Collocations — Cụm từ kết hợp tự nhiên A collocation is a pair or group of words that are often used together, for example make a decision and heavy rain. Collocation (cụm từ kết hợp) là những từ thường đi cùng nhau một cách tự nhiên; người bản ngữ không nói do a decision hay strong rain. make vs do — make thường dùng khi tạo ra một thứ mới: make a mistake, make progress, make a phone call. Do thường dùng cho hoạt động hoặc công việc: do homework, do the dishes, do research. take — take a photo (chụp ảnh), take a break (nghỉ giải lao), take a chance (thử vận may), take responsibility (chịu trách nhiệm).

Từ strongly đi với recommend, còn heavily đi với depend, như heavily depend on. Cách học collocation hiệu quả: hãy ghi cả cụm chứ không ghi từng từ riêng lẻ, và dùng collocation dictionary như Oxford Collocations Dictionary. When you read, underline word pairs that sound natural and copy them into your notebook. Lỗi thường gặp: dịch từng từ từ tiếng Việt sang tiếng Anh. Ví dụ người Việt hay nói open the light, nhưng người bản ngữ nói turn on the light.

take — take a photo (chụp ảnh), take a break (nghỉ giải lao), take a chance (thử vận may), take responsibility (chịu trách nhiệm). have — have a shower (tắm), have a look (xem qua), have a conversation (trò chuyện). In British English, people say have a shower, while Americans often say take a shower. Adjective + noun collocations: strong coffee (cà phê đậm), heavy traffic (giao thông đông đúc), fast food (đồ ăn nhanh). We say strong coffee but not powerful coffee, although powerful engine is correct. Verb + adverb collocations: strongly recommend, deeply regret, highly likely. Từ strongly đi với recommend, còn heavily đi với depend, như heavily depend on.
answer: A collocation is a pair or group of words that are often used together [1]. For example, make a decision and heavy rain [1].

context: Business Email Phrases — Cụm từ trong email công việc A professional email usually has five parts: a subject line, a greeting, an opening sentence, the main message and a closing. Một email công việc thường có năm phần: tiêu đề, lời chào, câu mở đầu, nội dung chính và lời kết. Subject line — Keep it under eight words and make it specific, for example Meeting request: project update on Thursday. Tiêu đề rõ ràng giúp người nhận quyết định mở thư nhanh hơn. Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together.

Tránh nói I attach the file without mentioning what it is. Nhớ kiểm tra tệp đính kèm trước khi bấm gửi. Closing — Best regards is the most common closing and is safe in most situations. Yours faithfully is used with Dear Sir or Madam, and Yours sincerely is used with a person's name. Thân mật hơn thì có thể dùng Kind regards. Tone — Avoid slang, capital letters for whole sentences and too many exclamation marks. Viết ngắn gọn: mỗi đoạn tối đa ba đến bốn câu. Before sending, read the email aloud once to check the tone and correct spelling mistakes.

(tôi viết thư để hỏi về...), Thank you for your prompt reply (cảm ơn bạn đã phản hồi nhanh). Requests — Could you please send me the report by Friday? is polite. answer: A professional email usually has five parts [1].

context: The IELTS Speaking Test The IELTS Speaking test is a face-to-face interview with a certified examiner and lasts between 11 and 14 minutes. It is recorded so that the result can be checked later. The test has three parts. In Part 1, which lasts four to five minutes, the examiner asks general questions about familiar topics such as home, family, work and hobbies. In Part 2 the candidate receives a task card with a topic and has one minute to prepare notes. The candidate then speaks for one to two minutes without interruption. The examiner stops the candidate after two minutes. Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes.

It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example. If a candidate does not understand a question, they may ask the examiner to repeat it, and this does not reduce the score. The speaking test can take place on the same day as the other sections or up to seven days before or after them.

Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes. The questions are more abstract and are connected to the topic in Part 2, for example asking the candidate to compare past and present or to predict the future. Four criteria are used for marking, and each is worth 25 percent of the score: fluency and coherence, lexical resource, grammatical range and accuracy, and pronunciation. Scores are given in bands from 0 to 9, and half bands such as 6.5 are allowed. Candidates are advised not to memorise answers, because examiners are trained to notice rehearsed language and it lowers the fluency score. It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example.

context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task. Deep creative work may need longer uninterrupted periods, so some people adjust the length to 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute break. The technique also encourages tracking. At the end of each day the learner counts how many pomodoros were completed, which gives a simple measure of effort.

This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins. If a distraction appears during a pomodoro, the worker writes it down on a separate list and returns to the task at once. A pomodoro that is interrupted cannot be counted, and it must be restarted from the beginning. Language learners use the method to study vocabulary, grammar or listening in short focused blocks. Many find that the fixed limit makes it easier to start, because the task feels smaller than a whole evening of study. Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task.

context: Word Families and Affixes A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. Learning a whole family at once is more efficient than learning each word separately. Most word families are built from a base word plus affixes. There are two kinds of affixes: prefixes, which come before the base, and suffixes, which come after it. For example, in the word unhappiness, un- is a prefix and -ness is a suffix. Prefixes usually change the meaning but not the part of speech. The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite.

Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text. Reaching 98 percent, which is considered comfortable for reading without a dictionary, requires about 8,000 to 9,000 word families. A common mistake is to assume that every affix works with every base. The word informal takes the prefix in-, but the correct opposites of possible and legal are impossible and illegal, because the prefix changes its spelling before the letters p and l. To practise, learners can choose a base word each day and write down as many family members as they can before checking a dictionary.

The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite. The prefix pre- means before, as in preview, and mis- means wrongly, as in misunderstand. Suffixes usually change the part of speech. The suffix -tion turns a verb into a noun, as in educate and education. The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb, as in quick and quickly, and -able makes an adjective from a verb, as in comfortable or readable. Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text.
answer: A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning [1].

context: The Shadowing Technique Shadowing is a language learning method in which the learner listens to a recording and repeats it aloud almost at the same time, staying only about one second behind the speaker. The method was popularised by the interpreter and professor Alexander Arguelles. The technique trains pronunciation, rhythm and intonation rather than vocabulary. Because the learner must copy the speaker's stress and pauses, the mouth muscles become used to the sounds of the language. There are two main forms. In no-text shadowing, the learner listens and repeats without reading anything. In text shadowing, the learner follows a transcript while speaking, which is easier and is recommended for beginners. A typical session has four steps.

Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly. Shadowing does not replace conversation. It improves accuracy of sound, but the learner still needs to speak with real people to practise choosing words quickly.

A typical session has four steps. First, listen to the audio once to understand the general meaning. Second, read the transcript and look up unknown words. Third, shadow the audio while reading the text. Fourth, shadow again without the text and record your own voice to compare it with the original. Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Clips of one to two minutes are long enough to be useful and short enough to repeat many times. Ten to fifteen minutes of daily practice is enough. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.
answer: The learner stays only about one second behind the speaker [1].

context: Mạo từ a, an và the trong tiếng Anh Mạo từ là từ đứng trước danh từ để cho biết danh từ đó xác định hay không xác định. Tiếng Anh có hai loại mạo từ: mạo từ không xác định gồm a và an, và mạo từ xác định là the. Ta dùng a trước từ bắt đầu bằng phụ âm và an trước từ bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm. Điều quan trọng là âm đọc chứ không phải chữ cái viết: ta nói an hour vì chữ h không được đọc, và nói a university vì từ này bắt đầu bằng âm /j/.

Ví dụ: Water is essential for life và Dogs are loyal animals. Với tên các bữa ăn, môn thể thao và môn học ta thường bỏ mạo từ, như have breakfast, play football và study mathematics. Một lỗi thường gặp của người Việt là bỏ quên mạo từ vì tiếng Việt không có hệ thống mạo từ tương ứng. Người học nên kiểm tra mọi danh từ đếm được số ít xem đã có a, an, the hoặc từ hạn định khác chưa.

Ví dụ: The dog was very friendly, vì con chó này đã được nhắc đến trước đó. Ta cũng dùng the với những vật duy nhất như the sun, the moon và the earth. The còn được dùng trước tên sông, biển, dãy núi và quần đảo, ví dụ the Mekong, the Pacific Ocean và the Alps. Tuy nhiên ta không dùng mạo từ trước tên hầu hết các quốc gia, thành phố và ngôn ngữ, như Vietnam, Hanoi hay English. Không dùng mạo từ trước danh từ không đếm được hoặc danh từ số nhiều khi nói chung chung. Ví dụ: Water is essential for life và Dogs are loyal animals.

context: Từ dễ nhầm lẫn — Confusing words Nhiều người học nhầm lẫn các cặp từ có cách viết hoặc âm đọc gần giống nhau. Many learners confuse pairs of words that look or sound similar. affect và effect — Affect thường là động từ nghĩa là ảnh hưởng đến: The weather affects my mood. Effect thường là danh từ nghĩa là tác động: The medicine had a good effect. its và it's — Its là tính từ sở hữu: The cat licked its paw. It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining.

advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/. Advise là động từ, đọc là /ədˈvaɪz/. Ta nói give some advice, không nói give an advice. Cách học: hãy viết một câu ví dụ riêng cho mỗi từ trong cặp và đọc to câu đó. Writing one example sentence for each word helps you remember the difference better than memorising a definition.

It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining. their, there và they're — Their chỉ sự sở hữu của họ, there chỉ nơi chốn, còn they're là viết tắt của they are. context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task. Deep creative work may need longer uninterrupted periods, so some people adjust the length to 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute break. The technique also encourages tracking. At the end of each day the learner counts how many pomodoros were completed, which gives a simple measure of effort.

This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins. If a distraction appears during a pomodoro, the worker writes it down on a separate list and returns to the task at once. A pomodoro that is interrupted cannot be counted, and it must be restarted from the beginning. Language learners use the method to study vocabulary, grammar or listening in short focused blocks. Many find that the fixed limit makes it easier to start, because the task feels smaller than a whole evening of study. Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task.
answer: Francesco Cirillo developed the Pomodoro Technique.

context: Word Families and Affixes A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. Learning a whole family at once is more efficient than learning each word separately. Most word families are built from a base word plus affixes. There are two kinds of affixes: prefixes, which come before the base, and suffixes, which come after it. For example, in the word unhappiness, un- is a prefix and -ness is a suffix. Prefixes usually change the meaning but not the part of speech. The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite.

Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text. Reaching 98 percent, which is considered comfortable for reading without a dictionary, requires about 8,000 to 9,000 word families. A common mistake is to assume that every affix works with every base. The word informal takes the prefix in-, but the correct opposites of possible and legal are impossible and illegal, because the prefix changes its spelling before the letters p and l. To practise, learners can choose a base word each day and write down as many family members as they can before checking a dictionary.

The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite. The prefix pre- means before, as in preview, and mis- means wrongly, as in misunderstand. Suffixes usually change the part of speech. The suffix -tion turns a verb into a noun, as in educate and education. The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb, as in quick and quickly, and -able makes an adjective from a verb, as in comfortable or readable. Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text.
answer: A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning.

context: The Shadowing Technique Shadowing is a language learning method in which the learner listens to a recording and repeats it aloud almost at the same time, staying only about one second behind the speaker. The method was popularised by the interpreter and professor Alexander Arguelles. The technique trains pronunciation, rhythm and intonation rather than vocabulary. Because the learner must copy the speaker's stress and pauses, the mouth muscles become used to the sounds of the language. There are two main forms. In no-text shadowing, the learner listens and repeats without reading anything. In text shadowing, the learner follows a transcript while speaking, which is easier and is recommended for beginners. A typical session has four steps.

Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly. Shadowing does not replace conversation. It improves accuracy of sound, but the learner still needs to speak with real people to practise choosing words quickly.

A typical session has four steps. First, listen to the audio once to understand the general meaning. Second, read the transcript and look up unknown words. Third, shadow the audio while reading the text. Fourth, shadow again without the text and record your own voice to compare it with the original. Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Clips of one to two minutes are long enough to be useful and short enough to repeat many times. Ten to fifteen minutes of daily practice is enough. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.
answer: About one second behind the speaker.

Điều quan trọng là âm đọc chứ không phải chữ cái viết: ta nói an hour vì chữ h không được đọc, và nói a university vì từ này bắt đầu bằng âm /j/.

context: Giới từ chỉ thời gian: in, on, at Ba giới từ in, on và at thường dùng để nói về thời gian. Cách dễ nhớ là hình dung một hình tháp ngược: in dùng cho khoảng thời gian dài, on cho ngày cụ thể và at cho thời điểm chính xác. Ta dùng in trước tháng, năm, mùa và các buổi trong ngày. Ví dụ: in July, in 2024, in summer và in the morning. Tuy nhiên với buổi đêm ta lại dùng at night. Ta dùng on trước các ngày trong tuần và ngày tháng cụ thể, ví dụ on Monday, on 5 May và on my birthday.

Ta dùng on trước các ngày trong tuần và ngày tháng cụ thể, ví dụ on Monday, on 5 May và on my birthday. Khi nói về một buổi cụ thể của một ngày, ta cũng dùng on, như on Friday evening. Ta dùng at trước giờ giấc và một số cụm cố định. Ví dụ: at 7 o'clock, at noon, at midnight và at the weekend trong tiếng Anh Anh. Người Mỹ thường nói on the weekend. Không dùng giới từ trước các từ như next, last, this, every và tomorrow. Ta nói I will see you next week, không nói in next week; và nói She calls me every day, không nói on every day.

Ta nói I will see you next week, không nói in next week; và nói She calls me every day, không nói on every day. Giới từ for chỉ khoảng thời gian, còn since chỉ mốc thời gian bắt đầu. Ví dụ: I have lived here for ten years và I have lived here since 2015. Giới từ by nghĩa là không muộn hơn một thời điểm, ví dụ: Please finish the report by Friday. Giới từ until nghĩa là kéo dài đến một thời điểm, ví dụ: I will wait until six. Một lỗi thường gặp là dùng in với ngày cụ thể. Câu in Monday là sai, câu đúng là on Monday.

context: Từ dễ nhầm lẫn — Confusing words Nhiều người học nhầm lẫn các cặp từ có cách viết hoặc âm đọc gần giống nhau. Many learners confuse pairs of words that look or sound similar. affect và effect — Affect thường là động từ nghĩa là ảnh hưởng đến: The weather affects my mood. Effect thường là danh từ nghĩa là tác động: The medicine had a good effect. its và it's — Its là tính từ sở hữu: The cat licked its paw. It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining.

advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/. Advise là động từ, đọc là /ədˈvaɪz/. Ta nói give some advice, không nói give an advice. Cách học: hãy viết một câu ví dụ riêng cho mỗi từ trong cặp và đọc to câu đó. Writing one example sentence for each word helps you remember the difference better than memorising a definition.

It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining. their, there và they're — Their chỉ sự sở hữu của họ, there chỉ nơi chốn, còn they're là viết tắt của they are. Example: They're putting their bags over there. then và than — Then chỉ thời gian hoặc thứ tự: First we ate, then we left. Than dùng để so sánh: She is taller than her brother. lose và loose — Lose /luːz/ là động từ, nghĩa là mất hoặc thua: Don't lose your keys. Loose /luːs/ là tính từ, nghĩa là lỏng: This shirt is too loose. advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/.
answer: Affect thường là động từ nghĩa là ảnh hưởng đến.

context: Business Email Phrases — Cụm từ trong email công việc A professional email usually has five parts: a subject line, a greeting, an opening sentence, the main message and a closing. Một email công việc thường có năm phần: tiêu đề, lời chào, câu mở đầu, nội dung chính và lời kết. Subject line — Keep it under eight words and make it specific, for example Meeting request: project update on Thursday. Tiêu đề rõ ràng giúp người nhận quyết định mở thư nhanh hơn. Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together.

Tránh nói I attach the file without mentioning what it is. Nhớ kiểm tra tệp đính kèm trước khi bấm gửi. Closing — Best regards is the most common closing and is safe in most situations. Yours faithfully is used with Dear Sir or Madam, and Yours sincerely is used with a person's name. Thân mật hơn thì có thể dùng Kind regards. Tone — Avoid slang, capital letters for whole sentences and too many exclamation marks. Viết ngắn gọn: mỗi đoạn tối đa ba đến bốn câu. Before sending, read the email aloud once to check the tone and correct spelling mistakes.

Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together. If you do not know the name, write Dear Sir or Madam, though many companies now prefer Dear Hiring Team. Opening — I am writing to inquire about... (tôi viết thư để hỏi về...), Thank you for your prompt reply (cảm ơn bạn đã phản hồi nhanh). Requests — Could you please send me the report by Friday? is polite. Từ please và could làm câu yêu cầu lịch sự hơn so với Send me the report. Attachments — Please find the attached file. Tránh nói I attach the file without mentioning what it is.
answer: A professional email usually has five parts: a subject line, a greeting, an opening sentence, the main message, and a closing.

context: The IELTS Speaking Test The IELTS Speaking test is a face-to-face interview with a certified examiner and lasts between 11 and 14 minutes. It is recorded so that the result can be checked later. The test has three parts. In Part 1, which lasts four to five minutes, the examiner asks general questions about familiar topics such as home, family, work and hobbies. In Part 2 the candidate receives a task card with a topic and has one minute to prepare notes. The candidate then speaks for one to two minutes without interruption. The examiner stops the candidate after two minutes. Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes.

It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example. If a candidate does not understand a question, they may ask the examiner to repeat it, and this does not reduce the score. The speaking test can take place on the same day as the other sections or up to seven days before or after them.

Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes. The questions are more abstract and are connected to the topic in Part 2, for example asking the candidate to compare past and present or to predict the future. Four criteria are used for marking, and each is worth 25 percent of the score: fluency and coherence, lexical resource, grammatical range and accuracy, and pronunciation. Scores are given in bands from 0 to 9, and half bands such as 6.5 are allowed. Candidates are advised not to memorise answers, because examiners are trained to notice rehearsed language and it lowers the fluency score. It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example.
answer: The IELTS Speaking test lasts between 11 and 14 minutes [1].

context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task. Deep creative work may need longer uninterrupted periods, so some people adjust the length to 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute break. The technique also encourages tracking. At the end of each day the learner counts how many pomodoros were completed, which gives a simple measure of effort.

This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins. If a distraction appears during a pomodoro, the worker writes it down on a separate list and returns to the task at once. A pomodoro that is interrupted cannot be counted, and it must be restarted from the beginning. Language learners use the method to study vocabulary, grammar or listening in short focused blocks. Many find that the fixed limit makes it easier to start, because the task feels smaller than a whole evening of study. Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task.
answer: Francesco Cirillo developed the Pomodoro Technique [1].

This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins. If a distraction appears during a pomodoro, the worker writes it down on a separate list and returns to the task at once. Many find that the fixed limit makes it easier to start, because the task feels smaller than a whole evening of study. Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task.

The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

context: Word Families and Affixes A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. Learning a whole family at once is more efficient than learning each word separately. Most word families are built from a base word plus affixes. There are two kinds of affixes: prefixes, which come before the base, and suffixes, which come after it. For example, in the word unhappiness, un- is a prefix and -ness is a suffix. Prefixes usually change the meaning but not the part of speech. The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite.

Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text. Reaching 98 percent, which is considered comfortable for reading without a dictionary, requires about 8,000 to 9,000 word families. A common mistake is to assume that every affix works with every base. The word informal takes the prefix in-, but the correct opposites of possible and legal are impossible and illegal, because the prefix changes its spelling before the letters p and l. To practise, learners can choose a base word each day and write down as many family members as they can before checking a dictionary.

The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite. The prefix pre- means before, as in preview, and mis- means wrongly, as in misunderstand. Suffixes usually change the part of speech. The suffix -tion turns a verb into a noun, as in educate and education. The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb, as in quick and quickly, and -able makes an adjective from a verb, as in comfortable or readable. Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text.

Hai mệnh đề có thể đổi chỗ cho nhau; khi mệnh đề if đứng đầu câu thì ta đặt dấu phẩy sau nó. Câu điều kiện loại 1 diễn tả điều kiện có thể xảy ra ở hiện tại hoặc tương lai. Cấu trúc là If + thì hiện tại đơn, S + will + động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home. Câu điều kiện loại 2 diễn tả điều kiện không có thật ở hiện tại hoặc rất khó xảy ra.

Câu điều kiện loại 2 diễn tả điều kiện không có thật ở hiện tại hoặc rất khó xảy ra. Cấu trúc là If + thì quá khứ đơn, S + would + động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ: If I had a million dollars, I would travel around the world. Trong câu điều kiện loại 2, động từ to be ở mệnh đề if thường dùng dạng were cho mọi chủ ngữ, kể cả I, he và she. Vì vậy ta nói If I were you, I would apologise, chứ không nói If I was you trong văn phong trang trọng. Không dùng will hoặc would trong mệnh đề if.

Ở mệnh đề chính, ngoài will và would ta có thể dùng các động từ khuyết thiếu khác như can, could, may hoặc might để diễn tả khả năng thấp hơn, ví dụ: If you practise every day, you might improve quickly. Từ unless có nghĩa là if not. Câu Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus có nghĩa giống như If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.

Ta dùng on trước các ngày trong tuần và ngày tháng cụ thể, ví dụ on Monday, on 5 May và on my birthday. Khi nói về một buổi cụ thể của một ngày, ta cũng dùng on, như on Friday evening. Ta dùng at trước giờ giấc và một số cụm cố định. Ví dụ: at 7 o'clock, at noon, at midnight và at the weekend trong tiếng Anh Anh. Người Mỹ thường nói on the weekend. Giới từ until nghĩa là kéo dài đến một thời điểm, ví dụ: I will wait until six. Một lỗi thường gặp là dùng in với ngày cụ thể. Câu in Monday là sai, câu đúng là on Monday.
answer: Hình tháp ngược giúp ghi nhớ cách sử dụng in, on và at như sau: in dùng cho khoảng thời gian dài, on cho ngày cụ thể và at cho thời điểm chính xác [1].

Cách học: hãy viết một câu ví dụ riêng cho mỗi từ trong cặp và đọc to câu đó. Writing one example sentence for each word helps you remember the difference better than memorising a definition.

context: Business Email Phrases — Cụm từ trong email công việc A professional email usually has five parts: a subject line, a greeting, an opening sentence, the main message and a closing. Một email công việc thường có năm phần: tiêu đề, lời chào, câu mở đầu, nội dung chính và lời kết. Subject line — Keep it under eight words and make it specific, for example Meeting request: project update on Thursday. Tiêu đề rõ ràng giúp người nhận quyết định mở thư nhanh hơn. Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together.

Tránh nói I attach the file without mentioning what it is. Nhớ kiểm tra tệp đính kèm trước khi bấm gửi. Closing — Best regards is the most common closing and is safe in most situations. Yours faithfully is used with Dear Sir or Madam, and Yours sincerely is used with a person's name. Thân mật hơn thì có thể dùng Kind regards. Tone — Avoid slang, capital letters for whole sentences and too many exclamation marks. Viết ngắn gọn: mỗi đoạn tối đa ba đến bốn câu. Before sending, read the email aloud once to check the tone and correct spelling mistakes.

Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together. If you do not know the name, write Dear Sir or Madam, though many companies now prefer Dear Hiring Team. Opening — I am writing to inquire about... (tôi viết thư để hỏi về...), Thank you for your prompt reply (cảm ơn bạn đã phản hồi nhanh). Requests — Could you please send me the report by Friday? is polite. Từ please và could làm câu yêu cầu lịch sự hơn so với Send me the report. Attachments — Please find the attached file. Tránh nói I attach the file without mentioning what it is.
answer: A professional email usually has five parts: a subject line, a greeting, an opening sentence, the main message and a closing [1].

context: The IELTS Speaking Test The IELTS Speaking test is a face-to-face interview with a certified examiner and lasts between 11 and 14 minutes. It is recorded so that the result can be checked later. The test has three parts. In Part 1, which lasts four to five minutes, the examiner asks general questions about familiar topics such as home, family, work and hobbies. In Part 2 the candidate receives a task card with a topic and has one minute to prepare notes. The candidate then speaks for one to two minutes without interruption. The examiner stops the candidate after two minutes. Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes.

It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example. If a candidate does not understand a question, they may ask the examiner to repeat it, and this does not reduce the score. The speaking test can take place on the same day as the other sections or up to seven days before or after them.

Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes. The questions are more abstract and are connected to the topic in Part 2, for example asking the candidate to compare past and present or to predict the future. Four criteria are used for marking, and each is worth 25 percent of the score: fluency and coherence, lexical resource, grammatical range and accuracy, and pronunciation. Scores are given in bands from 0 to 9, and half bands such as 6.5 are allowed. Candidates are advised not to memorise answers, because examiners are trained to notice rehearsed language and it lowers the fluency score. It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example.
answer: The IELTS Speaking test lasts between 11 and 14 minutes [1].

context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task. Deep creative work may need longer uninterrupted periods, so some people adjust the length to 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute break. The technique also encourages tracking. At the end of each day the learner counts how many pomodoros were completed, which gives a simple measure of effort.

This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins. If a distraction appears during a pomodoro, the worker writes it down on a separate list and returns to the task at once. A pomodoro that is interrupted cannot be counted, and it must be restarted from the beginning. Language learners use the method to study vocabulary, grammar or listening in short focused blocks. Many find that the fixed limit makes it easier to start, because the task feels smaller than a whole evening of study. Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task.
answer: Francesco Cirillo developed the Pomodoro Technique [1].

context: Word Families and Affixes A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. Learning a whole family at once is more efficient than learning each word separately. Most word families are built from a base word plus affixes. There are two kinds of affixes: prefixes, which come before the base, and suffixes, which come after it. For example, in the word unhappiness, un- is a prefix and -ness is a suffix. Prefixes usually change the meaning but not the part of speech. The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite.

Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text. Reaching 98 percent, which is considered comfortable for reading without a dictionary, requires about 8,000 to 9,000 word families. context: The Shadowing Technique Shadowing is a language learning method in which the learner listens to a recording and repeats it aloud almost at the same time, staying only about one second behind the speaker. The method was popularised by the interpreter and professor Alexander Arguelles. The technique trains pronunciation, rhythm and intonation rather than vocabulary. Because the learner must copy the speaker's stress and pauses, the mouth muscles become used to the sounds of the language. There are two main forms. In no-text shadowing, the learner listens and repeats without reading anything. In text shadowing, the learner follows a transcript while speaking, which is easier and is recommended for beginners. A typical session has four steps.

Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly. Shadowing does not replace conversation. It improves accuracy of sound, but the learner still needs to speak with real people to practise choosing words quickly.

A typical session has four steps. First, listen to the audio once to understand the general meaning. Second, read the transcript and look up unknown words. Third, shadow the audio while reading the text. Fourth, shadow again without the text and record your own voice to compare it with the original. Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Clips of one to two minutes are long enough to be useful and short enough to repeat many times. Ten to fifteen minutes of daily practice is enough. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.
answer: The learner stays only about one second behind the speaker [1].

The method was popularised by the interpreter and professor Alexander Arguelles. The technique trains pronunciation, rhythm and intonation rather than vocabulary. Because the learner must copy the speaker's stress and pauses, the mouth muscles become used to the sounds of the language. There are two main forms. In no-text shadowing, the learner listens and repeats without reading anything. In text shadowing, the learner follows a transcript while speaking, which is easier and is recommended for beginners. A typical session has four steps.

Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly. Shadowing does not replace conversation. It improves accuracy of sound, but the learner still needs to speak with real people to practise choosing words quickly.

A typical session has four steps. First, listen to the audio once to understand the general meaning. Second, read the transcript and look up unknown words. Third, shadow the audio while reading the text. Fourth, shadow again without the text and record your own voice to compare it with the original. Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Clips of one to two minutes are long enough to be useful and short enough to repeat many times. Ten to fifteen minutes of daily practice is enough. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.

context: Câu điều kiện loại 1 và loại 2 Câu điều kiện gồm hai mệnh đề: mệnh đề if nêu điều kiện và mệnh đề chính nêu kết quả. Hai mệnh đề có thể đổi chỗ cho nhau; khi mệnh đề if đứng đầu câu thì ta đặt dấu phẩy sau nó. Câu điều kiện loại 1 diễn tả điều kiện có thể xảy ra ở hiện tại hoặc tương lai. Cấu trúc là If + thì hiện tại đơn, S + will + động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home. Câu điều kiện loại 2 diễn tả điều kiện không có thật ở hiện tại hoặc rất khó xảy ra.

Câu điều kiện loại 2 diễn tả điều kiện không có thật ở hiện tại hoặc rất khó xảy ra. Cấu trúc là If + thì quá khứ đơn, S + would + động từ nguyên mẫu. Ví dụ: If I had a million dollars, I would travel around the world. Trong câu điều kiện loại 2, động từ to be ở mệnh đề if thường dùng dạng were cho mọi chủ ngữ, kể cả I, he và she. Vì vậy ta nói If I were you, I would apologise, chứ không nói If I was you trong văn phong trang trọng. Không dùng will hoặc would trong mệnh đề if.

Không dùng will hoặc would trong mệnh đề if. Câu If you will study hard, you pass là sai; câu đúng là If you study hard, you will pass. Ở mệnh đề chính, ngoài will và would ta có thể dùng các động từ khuyết thiếu khác như can, could, may hoặc might để diễn tả khả năng thấp hơn, ví dụ: If you practise every day, you might improve quickly. Từ unless có nghĩa là if not. Câu Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus có nghĩa giống như If you do not hurry, you will miss the bus.

context: Mạo từ a, an và the trong tiếng Anh Mạo từ là từ đứng trước danh từ để cho biết danh từ đó xác định hay không xác định. Tiếng Anh có hai loại mạo từ: mạo từ không xác định gồm a và an, và mạo từ xác định là the. Ta dùng a trước từ bắt đầu bằng phụ âm và an trước từ bắt đầu bằng nguyên âm. Điều quan trọng là âm đọc chứ không phải chữ cái viết: ta nói an hour vì chữ h không được đọc, và nói a university vì từ này bắt đầu bằng âm /j/.

Ví dụ: Water is essential for life và Dogs are loyal animals. Với tên các bữa ăn, môn thể thao và môn học ta thường bỏ mạo từ, như have breakfast, play football và study mathematics. Một lỗi thường gặp của người Việt là bỏ quên mạo từ vì tiếng Việt không có hệ thống mạo từ tương ứng. Người học nên kiểm tra mọi danh từ đếm được số ít xem đã có a, an, the hoặc từ hạn định khác chưa.

Ví dụ: The dog was very friendly, vì con chó này đã được nhắc đến trước đó. Ta cũng dùng the với những vật duy nhất như the sun, the moon và the earth. The còn được dùng trước tên sông, biển, dãy núi và quần đảo, ví dụ the Mekong, the Pacific Ocean và the Alps. Tuy nhiên ta không dùng mạo từ trước tên hầu hết các quốc gia, thành phố và ngôn ngữ, như Vietnam, Hanoi hay English. Không dùng mạo từ trước danh từ không đếm được hoặc danh từ số nhiều khi nói chung chung. Ví dụ: Water is essential for life và Dogs are loyal animals.

context: The IELTS Speaking Test The IELTS Speaking test is a face-to-face interview with a certified examiner and lasts between 11 and 14 minutes. It is recorded so that the result can be checked later. The test has three parts. In Part 1, which lasts four to five minutes, the examiner asks general questions about familiar topics such as home, family, work and hobbies. In Part 2 the candidate receives a task card with a topic and has one minute to prepare notes. The candidate then speaks for one to two minutes without interruption. The examiner stops the candidate after two minutes. Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes.

It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example. If a candidate does not understand a question, they may ask the examiner to repeat it, and this does not reduce the score. The speaking test can take place on the same day as the other sections or up to seven days before or after them.

Part 3 is a discussion of about four to five minutes. The questions are more abstract and are connected to the topic in Part 2, for example asking the candidate to compare past and present or to predict the future. Four criteria are used for marking, and each is worth 25 percent of the score: fluency and coherence, lexical resource, grammatical range and accuracy, and pronunciation. Scores are given in bands from 0 to 9, and half bands such as 6.5 are allowed. Candidates are advised not to memorise answers, because examiners are trained to notice rehearsed language and it lowers the fluency score. It is better to extend answers with a reason and an example.

context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. context: Word Families and Affixes A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. Learning a whole family at once is more efficient than learning each word separately. Most word families are built from a base word plus affixes. There are two kinds of affixes: prefixes, which come before the base, and suffixes, which come after it. For example, in the word unhappiness, un- is a prefix and -ness is a suffix. Prefixes usually change the meaning but not the part of speech. The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite.

Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text. Reaching 98 percent, which is considered comfortable for reading without a dictionary, requires about 8,000 to 9,000 word families. A common mistake is to assume that every affix works with every base. The word informal takes the prefix in-, but the correct opposites of possible and legal are impossible and illegal, because the prefix changes its spelling before the letters p and l. To practise, learners can choose a base word each day and write down as many family members as they can before checking a dictionary.

The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite. The prefix pre- means before, as in preview, and mis- means wrongly, as in misunderstand. Suffixes usually change the part of speech. The suffix -tion turns a verb into a noun, as in educate and education. The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb, as in quick and quickly, and -able makes an adjective from a verb, as in comfortable or readable. Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text.
answer: A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. They are often built from a base word plus affixes.

context: The Shadowing Technique Shadowing is a language learning method in which the learner listens to a recording and repeats it aloud almost at the same time, staying only about one second behind the speaker. The method was popularised by the interpreter and professor Alexander Arguelles. The technique trains pronunciation, rhythm and intonation rather than vocabulary. Because the learner must copy the speaker's stress and pauses, the mouth muscles become used to the sounds of the language. There are two main forms. In no-text shadowing, the learner listens and repeats without reading anything. In text shadowing, the learner follows a transcript while speaking, which is easier and is recommended for beginners. A typical session has four steps.

Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly. Shadowing does not replace conversation. It improves accuracy of sound, but the learner still needs to speak with real people to practise choosing words quickly.

A typical session has four steps. First, listen to the audio once to understand the general meaning. Second, read the transcript and look up unknown words. Third, shadow the audio while reading the text. Fourth, shadow again without the text and record your own voice to compare it with the original. Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Clips of one to two minutes are long enough to be useful and short enough to repeat many times. Ten to fifteen minutes of daily practice is enough. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.
answer: The learner stays about one second behind the speaker when shadowing. (Source: First excerpt)

Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.

answer: In, on, and at are time indicators in the Vietnamese language. They can be remembered easily with the image of an upside-down tower: "in" is used for longer periods of time (like months, years, seasons, and parts of the day), "on" is used for specific days of the week and specific dates, and "at" is used for exact times. For example, "in July," "in 2024," "in summer," and "in the morning" use "in." However, for the night, we use "at night." We use "on" before specific days of the week, specific dates, and personal dates, like "on Monday," "on 5 May," and "on my birthday." For a specific part of a day, we also use "on," like "on Friday evening." We use "at" before specific hours and some fixed phrases, such as "at 7 o'clock," "at noon," "at midnight," and "at the weekend" in English. Americans often say "on the weekend." We don't use a word before words like "next," "last," "this," "every," and "tomorrow." For example, we say "I will see you next week," not "in next week," and "She calls me every day," not "on every day."

context: Từ dễ nhầm lẫn — Confusing words Nhiều người học nhầm lẫn các cặp từ có cách viết hoặc âm đọc gần giống nhau. Many learners confuse pairs of words that look or sound similar. affect và effect — Affect thường là động từ nghĩa là ảnh hưởng đến: The weather affects my mood. Effect thường là danh từ nghĩa là tác động: The medicine had a good effect. its và it's — Its là tính từ sở hữu: The cat licked its paw. It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining.

advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/. Advise là động từ, đọc là /ədˈvaɪz/. Ta nói give some advice, không nói give an advice. Cách học: hãy viết một câu ví dụ riêng cho mỗi từ trong cặp và đọc to câu đó. Writing one example sentence for each word helps you remember the difference better than memorising a definition.

It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining. their, there và they're — Their chỉ sự sở hữu của họ, there chỉ nơi chốn, còn they're là viết tắt của they are. Example: They're putting their bags over there. then và than — Then chỉ thời gian hoặc thứ tự: First we ate, then we left. Than dùng để so sánh: She is taller than her brother. lose và loose — Lose /luːz/ là động từ, nghĩa là mất hoặc thua: Don't lose your keys. Loose /luːs/ là tính từ, nghĩa là lỏng: This shirt is too loose. advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/.
answer: The verb 'affect' means to influence or have an effect on. For example: "The weather affects my mood."

A resignation email should have the following structure:

1. Subject line: Resignation - [Your Name]
2. Greeting: Depending on your relationship with the recipient, you can use either "Dear [Recipient's Name]" or "Dear Hiring Manager." If you don't know the recipient's name, use "Dear Sir or Madam."
3. Opening: State the purpose of the email, such as "I am writing to formally resign from my position at [Company Name]."
4. Main message: Briefly explain the reasons for your resignation, express gratitude for the opportunities you've had, and give your notice period.
5. Closing: Use "Yours sincerely" if you've been addressed by a person's name, or "Best regards" if you haven't.
6. Signature: Include your full name, contact information, and the date.

context: The Pomodoro Technique The Pomodoro Technique is a time management method developed by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s. Cirillo named it after the tomato-shaped kitchen timer he used as a university student; pomodoro is the Italian word for tomato. The basic cycle has five steps. First, choose one task. Second, set a timer for 25 minutes and work on the task without interruption. Third, when the timer rings, take a short break of five minutes. Each 25-minute work period is called one pomodoro. After four pomodoros in a row, the worker takes a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes. This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins.

Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task. Deep creative work may need longer uninterrupted periods, so some people adjust the length to 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute break. The technique also encourages tracking. At the end of each day the learner counts how many pomodoros were completed, which gives a simple measure of effort.

This longer break lets the brain rest before the next set of cycles begins. If a distraction appears during a pomodoro, the worker writes it down on a separate list and returns to the task at once. A pomodoro that is interrupted cannot be counted, and it must be restarted from the beginning. Language learners use the method to study vocabulary, grammar or listening in short focused blocks. Many find that the fixed limit makes it easier to start, because the task feels smaller than a whole evening of study. Critics note that 25 minutes is not ideal for every task.
answer: Francesco Cirillo [1].

context: Word Families and Affixes A word family is a group of words that share the same base and are related in meaning, such as decide, decision, decisive and indecisive. Learning a whole family at once is more efficient than learning each word separately. Most word families are built from a base word plus affixes. There are two kinds of affixes: prefixes, which come before the base, and suffixes, which come after it. For example, in the word unhappiness, un- is a prefix and -ness is a suffix. Prefixes usually change the meaning but not the part of speech. The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite.

Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text. Reaching 98 percent, which is considered comfortable for reading without a dictionary, requires about 8,000 to 9,000 word families. A common mistake is to assume that every affix works with every base. The word informal takes the prefix in-, but the correct opposites of possible and legal are impossible and illegal, because the prefix changes its spelling before the letters p and l. To practise, learners can choose a base word each day and write down as many family members as they can before checking a dictionary.

The prefix un- often means not, as in unable, and re- means again, as in rewrite. The prefix pre- means before, as in preview, and mis- means wrongly, as in misunderstand. Suffixes usually change the part of speech. The suffix -tion turns a verb into a noun, as in educate and education. The suffix -ly turns an adjective into an adverb, as in quick and quickly, and -able makes an adjective from a verb, as in comfortable or readable. Researchers such as Paul Nation suggest that a learner who knows about 3,000 word families can understand roughly 95 percent of the words in an everyday text.

context: The Shadowing Technique Shadowing is a language learning method in which the learner listens to a recording and repeats it aloud almost at the same time, staying only about one second behind the speaker. The method was popularised by the interpreter and professor Alexander Arguelles. The technique trains pronunciation, rhythm and intonation rather than vocabulary. Because the learner must copy the speaker's stress and pauses, the mouth muscles become used to the sounds of the language. There are two main forms. In no-text shadowing, the learner listens and repeats without reading anything. In text shadowing, the learner follows a transcript while speaking, which is easier and is recommended for beginners. A typical session has four steps.

Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly. Shadowing does not replace conversation. It improves accuracy of sound, but the learner still needs to speak with real people to practise choosing words quickly.

A typical session has four steps. First, listen to the audio once to understand the general meaning. Second, read the transcript and look up unknown words. Third, shadow the audio while reading the text. Fourth, shadow again without the text and record your own voice to compare it with the original. Experts advise choosing audio that is slightly below the learner's listening level, at about 90 percent comprehension, so that attention can go to the sounds. Clips of one to two minutes are long enough to be useful and short enough to repeat many times. Ten to fifteen minutes of daily practice is enough. Longer sessions cause fatigue, and tired learners tend to copy the sounds carelessly.
answer: The learner stays about one second behind the speaker [1].

It is also used before names of rivers, seas, mountain ranges, and archipelagos, such as the Mekong, the Pacific Ocean, and the Alps. However, it is not used before most countries, cities, and languages, like Vietnam, Hanoi, or English [1]. We do not use "the" with uncountable nouns or plural countable nouns in general statements. For example: Water is essential for life and Dogs are loyal animals [1]. With names of meals, sports, and subjects, we usually omit the definite article, such as have breakfast, play football, and study mathematics [3]. A common mistake among Vietnamese speakers is forgetting to use "the" because Vietnamese does not have a corresponding system of definite articles. Learners should check every countable noun that is counted with a small number to see if it already has "a", "an", "the", or another limiting term [3].

Many learners confuse pairs of words that look or sound similar. affect và effect — Affect thường là động từ nghĩa là ảnh hưởng đến: The weather affects my mood. Effect thường là danh từ nghĩa là tác động: The medicine had a good effect. its và it's — Its là tính từ sở hữu: The cat licked its paw. It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining.

advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/. Advise là động từ, đọc là /ədˈvaɪz/. Ta nói give some advice, không nói give an advice. Cách học: hãy viết một câu ví dụ riêng cho mỗi từ trong cặp và đọc to câu đó. Writing one example sentence for each word helps you remember the difference better than memorising a definition.

It's là dạng viết tắt của it is hoặc it has: It's raining. their, there và they're — Their chỉ sự sở hữu của họ, there chỉ nơi chốn, còn they're là viết tắt của they are. Example: They're putting their bags over there. then và than — Then chỉ thời gian hoặc thứ tự: First we ate, then we left. Than dùng để so sánh: She is taller than her brother. lose và loose — Lose /luːz/ là động từ, nghĩa là mất hoặc thua: Don't lose your keys. Loose /luːs/ là tính từ, nghĩa là lỏng: This shirt is too loose. advice và advise — Advice là danh từ không đếm được, đọc là /ədˈvaɪs/.

context: Business Email Phrases — Cụm từ trong email công việc A professional email usually has five parts: a subject line, a greeting, an opening sentence, the main message and a closing. Một email công việc thường có năm phần: tiêu đề, lời chào, câu mở đầu, nội dung chính và lời kết. Subject line — Keep it under eight words and make it specific, for example Meeting request: project update on Thursday. Tiêu đề rõ ràng giúp người nhận quyết định mở thư nhanh hơn. Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together.

Tránh nói I attach the file without mentioning what it is. Nhớ kiểm tra tệp đính kèm trước khi bấm gửi. Closing — Best regards is the most common closing and is safe in most situations. Yours faithfully is used with Dear Sir or Madam, and Yours sincerely is used with a person's name. Thân mật hơn thì có thể dùng Kind regards. Tone — Avoid slang, capital letters for whole sentences and too many exclamation marks. Viết ngắn gọn: mỗi đoạn tối đa ba đến bốn câu. Before sending, read the email aloud once to check the tone and correct spelling mistakes.

Greeting — Use Dear Ms Nguyen when you do not know the person well, and Hi Minh when you already work together. If you do not know the name, write Dear Sir or Madam, though many companies now prefer Dear Hiring Team. Opening — I am writing to inquire about...
